Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-transcribe-medium-0203", "row_sha256": "d1000b7a59d8d3ddc99529b2d029eb6906ea8b036d83975f688a8d4b430fad4a", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "for today's notebook entry record the bedding measurements at A122 no sorry I mean B83 on the north side of the old quarry where the thin limestone beds dip toward the creek. Tess is taking the compass readings while I sketch the contact with the darker shale so note that the sketch is mine and the readings are hers. start at 2:15 this afternoon after we finish checking the loose blocks beside the trail and write down the strike before the dip so we use the same order as yesterday. the surface is damp from last night's rain and the lower ledge has a narrow band of rusty staining don't call that band an iron seam unless we can trace it across the face. add the hand lens and scale bar to the equipment list then leave a blank line for the sample number because we haven't collected a specimen yet. if the light changes before we finish take one overview photograph from the trail and note the time but don't move the flagging at the contact. at the end remind me to compare this sketch with the west-wall page in the notebook.", "output": "For today's notebook entry, record the bedding measurements at B83 on the north side of the old quarry, where the thin limestone beds dip toward the creek. Tess is taking the compass readings while I sketch the contact with the darker shale, so note that the sketch is mine and the readings are hers. Start at 2:15 this afternoon, after we finish checking the loose blocks beside the trail, and write down the strike before the dip so we use the same order as yesterday. The surface is damp from last night's rain, and the lower ledge has a narrow band of rusty staining. Don't call that band an iron seam unless we can trace it across the face. Add the hand lens and scale bar to the equipment list, then leave a blank line for the sample number because we haven't collected a specimen yet. If the light changes before we finish, take one overview photograph from the trail and note the time, but don't move the flagging at the contact. At the end, remind me to compare this sketch with the west-wall page in the notebook."}]
